decisions.rationale: id has distinct_count 10760 equal to dataset.row_count 10760 and null_rate 0.0, making it the only column that plausibly identifies one runway-end-pair row on its own.
dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across dataset.row_count 10760 rows, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is proposed.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry only ingestion bookkeeping (a single constant '{}' for _airbyte_meta), so they are dropped.

le_latitude_deg, le_longitude_deg, he_latitude_deg, and he_longitude_deg all land as oversized DECIMAL(38,9) but their min/max ranges (-179.881256 to 179.338837 and similar) fit comfortably in DECIMAL(9,6), the standard coordinate precision.

length_ft, width_ft, le_elevation_ft, he_elevation_ft, le_displaced_threshold_ft, and he_displaced_threshold_ft all show only whole-number sample values despite landing as DECIMAL(38,9), so they are cast to INTEGER.
le_heading_degt samples include fractional values such as 1.12 and 0.2, so unlike the other DECIMAL(38,9) measures it is cast to DECIMAL(5,2) rather than INTEGER.
lighted and closed each have distinct_count 2 with distinct_values exactly [0.0, 1.0] and null_rate 0.0, a clean binary signal suitable for BOOLEAN.

le_displaced_threshold_ft (null_rate 0.884201) and he_displaced_threshold_ft (null_rate 0.899907) are sparsely populated because displaced thresholds only apply to some runway ends, so both are retained nullable rather than dropped or imputed.

purpose: This table provides one row per runway end-pair record (keyed by id) describing a runway at an airport, including its physical dimensions, surface, lighting/closure status, and the geographic position, elevation, and heading of each of its two ends (low-end 'le_' and high-end 'he_'), feeding downstream airport infrastructure and flight-planning analytics.
usage: Join on airport_ref or airport_ident to the airports table to resolve full airport context; consumers must treat le_* and he_* latitude/longitude/elevation/heading/displaced-threshold columns as independently nullable (null rates between 0.22 and 0.90) and filter or handle nulls explicitly rather than assuming both runway ends are always populated; the closed boolean should be checked before treating a runway as active.
limitations: Geographic and physical attributes for runway ends are frequently missing (le_/he_ latitude and longitude null_rate around 0.22, elevation around 0.276, displaced thresholds 0.88-0.90), and these gaps were not imputed; le_ident and he_ident contain a handful of anomalous placeholder values ('.', '-', '-12') that were not corrected; airport_ref and airport_ident are retained as text and not validated against the airports table in this cleanup.
